title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous page). A 'Lie system' is a configuration (π ⊂ 𝔊 ⊂ M; π_0 ⊂ 𝔊_0). The most plausible reading is that 𝔊 is a profinite geometric fundamental group (for instance of a moduli stack or curve), 𝔊_0 a discrete model of it (orbifold π_1, e.g. a mapping class group), and M an 'arithmetic' extension (e.g. π_1 over Q, an extension of Gal(Q̄/Q)) acting on 𝔊 by conjugation. Section (65) gives a homomorphism φ: 𝔊_0 → 𝔊(Q) into the rational points of a linear algebraic group 𝔊_Q (e.g. the Zariski closure, a Sp_{2g}-type hull). By continuity φ extends to φ̂: 𝔊 → 𝔊(𝔸_Q), with 𝔸_Q presumably the (finite) adèles. On the previous page Grothendieck took the case where φ comes from a morphism of Lie systems M → M(𝔸_Q). There he built a natural algebraic group M^φ_Q, receiving 𝔊_Q via inner action and injective when the centre of 𝔊_Q is trivial. This realises 𝔊_Q inside a universal Lie system (Π ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M^φ_Q) attached to φ.

This page: when no such ambient morphism is assumed, it is not automatic that there is a homomorphism (73) φ_M: M → M^φ_Q(𝔸_Q) accounting for the action of M on 𝔊. Concretely one asks that for every g ∈ M the square (74) commute: φ̂ ∘ int(g)|𝔊 = int(φ_M(g))|𝔊(𝔸_Q) ∘ φ̂. Equivalently, the outer action of M on 𝔊 must be realised, through φ̂, by conjugation by adelic points of the universal algebraic group M^φ_Q. Grothendieck declares that he will mainly study those φ for which (73) exists, at least after restricting to an open subgroup of M. In other words, he singles out representations of the geometric fundamental group whose Galois/arithmetic conjugates are realised algebraically (adelically), up to finite index. This prepares an 'algebraic hull with arithmetic action' of the geometric π_1. The paradigm is π_1(M_{g,n}) → Sp_{2g}(Z) ⊂ Sp(Q), extended to π_1(M_{g,n}/Q) → GSp(𝔸_f) via the cyclotomic character. The next page then moves to differentiable actions and special Teichmüller groups.
errors: No mathematical error; the page states a condition rather than proving anything. Implicitly φ_M is only determined up to the centralizer of φ̂(𝔊) in M^φ_Q(𝔸_Q). It is unique only if that centralizer is trivial, which matches the trivial-centre hypothesis of the previous page; uniqueness and homomorphy are not discussed. The phrase 'restreindre à un sous-groupe ouvert' signals that only an open subgroup may stabilise the conjugacy class of φ.

ideas.what: Condition that the conjugation action of the arithmetic group M on the profinite geometric group 𝔊 be realised, via the adelic extension φ̂ of a rational representation φ, by conjugation by adelic points of an algebraic group M^φ_Q (diagram (74)).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on relative (algebraic/Malcev) completion of π_1; Galois-stable or 'arithmetic' representations of the geometric fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain–Matsumoto (relative and weighted completions with Galois action, c. 2003–2009); arithmetic local systems: Simpson, Esnault–Kerz, Petrov, Litt (2010s–2020s)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche material as far as known; unsure

ideas.what: Restricting to an open subgroup of M so that the action becomes algebraic (only finite-index stabiliser of the conjugacy class of φ).
ideas.modern_name: Representations whose isomorphism class is fixed by an open subgroup of Galois (descend to a finite extension)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in theory of arithmetic local systems

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates, as the main class of interest, representations φ of the discrete/profinite geometric π_1 into an algebraic group whose arithmetic outer action extends (after open restriction) to adelic points of a universal algebraic hull M^φ_Q. This is essentially the notion later studied as relative completion with Galois action (Hain–Matsumoto) and as arithmetic/Galois-invariant local systems. Here it is placed inside his Lie-system (π ⊂ 𝔊 ⊂ M) formalism aimed at Teichmüller towers.
missed.quote: On s'intéressera surtout aux φ (65) pour lesquels (73) existe — au moins quitte à restreindre à un sous-groupe ouvert de M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck anticipated the use of algebraic hulls of mapping class groups, with Galois action, as a tool for Galois–Teichmüller theory. He framed it adelically and universally (the group M^φ_Q) rather than ℓ-adically, a framing not standard in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up the adelic, algebraic-hull version of Galois actions on geometric fundamental groups, an early version of ideas credited to Hain–Matsumoto and to the theory of arithmetic local systems. It is only a definition/condition with no result, and the concept is now well developed.
